items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: you can get Jeb Patton, you can get Tadataka, you know there are guys out there.

ctx.x: That’s what you said pretty much 23 years ago when we met. I had asked you the question what are your goals in, I said, 15 years. But you said that, that you wanted to keep doing what you’re doing, do it better, be more organized, make some better bread.

So I think the organization part, that part changed my life. I did finally get a stage plot that works. I got the lists of all the different shows that I can do. There’s a big band show, there’s a four horn show, there’s orchestra shows. But the biggest part of the organization was having the charts — a readable chart — which took me forever. I was a bad chart writer and I finally, you know here I still even have this from Jessica’s show the other day. But I didn’t realize, I mean I used to really be — what am I…
Are your charts chord charts with cues for riffs and breaks and that kind of thing? © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
